strings.initialize.field.auth_method_hint: The shared key assumes it's already authorized on the device (e.g. preseeded via RPi Imager) — see Settings for the public key. Password is only used for this one run and is never stored.
strings.initialize.field.device_name_hint: Set as the device's hostname and /etc/hosts entry.
strings.initialize.field.netbird_setup_key_hint: Optional — installs NetBird either way; a setup key also joins it to your network right away. Get one from your NetBird management console. Never stored.
strings.initialize.field.password_hint: Only used if "Password" is selected above, and only for this one run — not stored. Entering a non-root user here also uses this as the sudo password.
strings.initialize.field.username_hint: root, or any other account — everything is run via sudo when this isn't root.
strings.initialize.fingerprint_note: SSH host key fingerprint presented by the device (trusted on this first connection — note it down if you want to verify it independently):
strings.initialize.intro: Provisions a brand new Raspberry Pi OS 13 device into a working OpenCanary honeypot over SSH — packages, the OpenCanary venv and service, locale/timezone, NetBird, and the portscan/Samba modules' host-side setup. Run this once, then add the device on the Honeypots page.
